title: Báo cáo sự cố (postmortem): sập cơ sở dữ liệu

materials.title: Postmortem
materials.body:
Incident summary — Checkout outage, 14 Oct 2026

What happened: From 20:05 to 21:10, customers could not complete payments. A database migration added an index to the orders table during peak hours. The table was locked for 65 minutes, and checkout requests timed out.

Impact: about 9,800 failed orders, estimated $310,000 in lost sales. No data was lost.

Detection: Alerts fired after 12 minutes because the error threshold was set too high.

Root cause: The migration was not reviewed for locking behaviour and was run without a maintenance window.

Actions: (1) run schema changes only with online migration tools; (2) lower the checkout error alert threshold; (3) add a 'risky migration' checklist to code review.

title: Bài blog: vì sao chúng tôi quay lại kiến trúc monolith

materials.title: Engineering blog
materials.body:
Three years ago we split our product into 40 microservices. Last quarter we merged most of them back into a modular monolith. Here is why.

First, our team is only 18 engineers. Each service had its own pipeline, alerts and on-call rotation, so we spent about 30% of our time on infrastructure instead of features. Second, many features touched five or six services, which made releases slow and debugging painful. Third, our cloud bill was high because each service ran with spare capacity.

The monolith is not a step back. We kept clear module boundaries, one database schema per module, and we still run two services separately: search and video processing, because they scale very differently.

Since the change, deployment time dropped from 45 to 12 minutes and incidents fell by 40%. Microservices solve organisational problems of large companies. For a small team, they can create more problems than they solve.

Internal memo: Using AI assistants at work (v1.2)

1. Allowed: drafting emails, summarising public documents, explaining code, writing unit tests.
2. Not allowed: pasting customer personal data, passwords, API keys or unreleased financial results into external AI tools.
3. All AI-generated code must be reviewed by a human and pass normal tests before merge.

title: Bài báo: fine-tuning LLM hiệu quả với LoRA

materials.title: Abstract
materials.body: Abstract. Fine-tuning large language models for a specific domain is expensive because all parameters must be updated. We study low-rank adaptation (LoRA) for legal question answering in Vietnamese. We fine-tune a 7B-parameter model by training only 0.3% of its parameters. On our new benchmark of 2,400 legal questions, LoRA reaches 78.4% accuracy, compared with 79.1% for full fine-tuning and 61.2% for the base model, while using 6x less GPU memory and 4x less training time. However, performance drops on questions that require reasoning across several laws. We release our dataset and code.

title: Bài báo: dự báo nhu cầu điện bằng Transformer

materials.title: Abstract
materials.body: Abstract. Accurate short-term electricity demand forecasting helps grid operators reduce costs. We compare a Transformer-based model with LSTM and gradient boosting on 5 years of hourly demand data from three cities, using weather and holiday features. The Transformer achieves the lowest error for 24-hour forecasts (MAPE 3.1% vs. 3.8% for LSTM), but gradient boosting is best for 1-hour forecasts and trains 20 times faster. All models perform poorly during extreme heat waves, which are rare in the training data. We suggest combining models depending on the forecast horizon.

title: Bài báo: thiên lệch trong mô hình chấm điểm tín dụng

materials.title: Abstract
materials.body: Abstract. Machine learning models are widely used to approve loans. We audit a credit scoring model used by a mid-sized lender on 120,000 applications. Although the model does not use gender as an input, approval rates differ: 64% for men and 55% for women with similar income and credit history. We find that features such as job title and shopping categories act as proxies for gender. Removing these features reduces the gap to 2 percentage points while lowering overall accuracy by only 0.8%. We recommend regular fairness audits before and after deployment.
